solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Government committee and department overseeing underwear

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece overseeing another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: CO is a government-department abbreviation, as in the old Colonial Office or Crown Office
a bra is an item of women's underwear

explanation.surface: A Whitehall committee and ministry keeping a watchful eye on lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: COBRA is the UK government's emergency committee, named after Cabinet Office Briefing Room A.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Cabinet Office briefing room where it meets, this is Britain's crisis response committee.

clue.text: Scottish well

parts.note: the Scots word for healthy-looking or fine, a near literal description rather than wordplay

explanation.walkthrough: Barely cryptic: 'well' could be a source of water, but here it means in good health, as the Scots say.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots usage the word describes someone fine, pretty and in good health.

clue.text: Subsidiary operation on railway branch

definitions.meaning: a secondary business or activity carried on beside the main one
a minor branch track off the main railway route

explanation.surface: Railway jargon for a minor operation running on a branch track.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of something running alongside the main business or main track.

clue.text: Where past customs are on the way out

definitions.text: Where past customs are on the way out

parts.words: Where past customs are on the way out
parts.note: sounds like traditions dying out, but describes the departures area of an airport beyond passport and customs control

explanation.surface: Old traditions are fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past customs' reads as old traditions; it really means having gone through customs, and 'on the way out' means departing on a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport, this is the zone beyond security and customs where departing passengers wait for flights.

clue.text: Shopping area for daughter's private time to enjoy

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter; the 's stands for has
something private is your own
to enjoy a right or benefit is to own it, to have the use of it

explanation.surface: A shopping district is where a daughter goes for some time to herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enjoy' is the verb own, in the sense of enjoying possession of something.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the central district of a city, with its stores and offices, is the shopping hub.

clue.text: Rein in on recycled 32 equipment

definitions.note: 32 refers to the answer at 32-across, the sport of golf

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and made into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to restrain reuse of some equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: '32' points to 32-across, GOLF, so the definition is golf equipment: a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with a steeply angled face, carried in every standard set, is a piece of golfing kit.

clue.text: Escapologist's distraction

indicators.note: the possessive says the answer belongs to, and so is found within, the word escapologist

explanation.surface: Something that diverts the attention of a Houdini figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is read as 'part of': the answer sits inside escaPOLOgist.
explanation.definitionFit: A game played on horseback is a pastime, and a pastime is a distraction from everyday life.

clue.text: Lives on income support on river

indicators.note: one piece placed on the other, joining them

parts.note: someone who lives is, exists
IS is the abbreviation for Income Support, a UK state benefit

explanation.surface: Someone surviving on state benefit beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Income Support is a UK means-tested benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames as it flows through Oxford is traditionally given this name.

clue.text: One comes to gardens endlessly researching

indicators.note: without its ends, so the first and last letters of the synonym are removed

parts.note: researching something is probing it

explanation.surface: Someone keeps turning up in gardens, forever doing research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips both ends from PROBING.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar garden bird that comes close to gardeners digging over the soil.

clue.text: Norwegian returns note; look!

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: FA is a note of the sol-fa scale
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: A Norwegian sends back a note, with a cry to look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns FA plus LO backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Norwegian man's name, borne by several kings of Norway.

clue.text: Royals seeking special noble

indicators.note: the first piece goes looking for the second and joins it

parts.note: princes are members of a royal family

explanation.surface: Members of a royal family looking for a special aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A king's daughter holds noble rank, so she is a noblewoman by birth.

clue.text: Cleaner lacking some energy becomes soldier

indicators.note: becomes signals a change of form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lacking means without, so a letter is removed from the word Cleaner

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy; some means just one of them

explanation.surface: A cleaner who has lost some vigour joins the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes one E from CLEANER, leaving CLANER, which 'becomes' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry trooper armed with a long lance was a type of soldier.

clue.text: Mountain dweller you expect to introduce first

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A mountaineer predicts an introduction of a creature to come first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' at the end takes the initial letters of 'you expect to introduce'.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman is said to live high in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Irish house admitting salute, in turn, for Welsh symbol

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: in turn means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to doff one's hat is to salute

explanation.surface: An Irish home takes in a greeting before a Welsh emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament. Doffing a hat is a salute; 'in turn' reverses it before 'admitting' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow spring flower is a national emblem of Wales, worn on St David's Day.

clue.text: See 6
Spooner's conundrum; Greek's 6th, or 7th after English final?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the T and Z sounds of the synonym change places

parts.note: a conundrum is a puzzle, a teaser, said as two syllables whose opening sounds are T and Z
the second syllable of the word teaser, pronounced with a Z sound, whose opening sound Spooner moves to the front

explanation.surface: A puzzle by Spooner about Greek letters and the English alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: Said as tee-zer, the synonym swaps its T and Z sounds. The definition sits mid-clue; 'or 7th after English final' is a second route: eta, the seventh Greek letter, after Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting alpha, beta, gamma, delta, epsilon, the next letter of that alphabet is the sixth.

clue.text: Twisting, unending street in Kabul's outskirts, home to bird of prey

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so the first and last letters are taken
twisting distorts the shape, so these letters are rearranged
unending means without its end, so the last letter of street goes

explanation.surface: A winding street in an Afghan city's suburbs where a raptor lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' drops the final T before 'Twisting' rearranges STREE into ESTRE; 'in' puts that inside the 'outskirts' of Kabul.
explanation.definitionFit: A small falcon that hovers before swooping is a hunting raptor.

clue.text: Leaves in place meal for 6, 15 carrier

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal
the answers at 6 and 15 make a golf club, and the person who carries a golfer's clubs is a caddie

explanation.surface: Somebody departs in a place where a meal is served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun: tea leaves, kept in this container.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tin or box is the place where loose tea leaves are stored.

clue.text: Cat lover, so it's said, first to describe spirit

indicators.note: first puts the second piece ahead of the first
so it's said means the word is heard rather than read, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a fan is a devoted lover of something
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A cat enthusiast is said to be first to describe a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so it's said' turns FAN into PHAN, which 'first' places ahead of TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition or ghost is a spirit, as in the Phantom of the Opera.

clue.text: One dons headgear for Scotsman's island race

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the second piece goes inside the first like a head inside a hat

parts.note: a hat is headgear
one is I, the Roman numeral
Ian is a typical Scottish name, Ian's in the possessive

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a Scotsman's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' places I inside HAT, then Ian's follows as a stock Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of a Caribbean island nation form one national group or race.

clue.text: See laws broken by treasonous people

indicators.note: broken means shattered into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Traitors are seen breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the letters of SEE LAWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacherous, sneaky people are called by the name of a small sly carnivore.

clue.text: Row on river in the south of France

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge
to row is to quarrel, to argue

explanation.surface: A dispute takes place on a river in southern France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam is the river of Cambridge. The definition is a description, a region lying in the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: This marshy Rhône delta region is located in southern France, so the clue's location phrase describes it.

clue.text: They may be looked up to in the cheap seats

definitions.text: They may be looked up to

definitions.meaning: the top gallery of a theatre, highest and cheapest

explanation.surface: Those in the theatre's cheapest seats may be the ones everyone looks up at.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine beings are revered, and the topmost theatre gallery is known by the same plural name.

clue.text: Impression of middleman ignores anything odd

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-placed letters leaves only the even ones, second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A broker's view, ignoring anything strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores anything odd' keeps the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of middleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or vague impression of something is a thought formed in the mind.

clue.text: Six of the children ought to be sufficient

indicators.note: six of the letters, taken in a run from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Half a dozen kids should be plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six of' takes six consecutive letters from childrEN OUGHt.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty or adequate in amount is a straight synonym of sufficient.

clue.text: Go up to reach the hierarchy

definitions.meaning: to climb or ascend, as a wall or a mountain
a graded system of ranks or levels

explanation.surface: Climb to reach the top of the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: One can climb up a wall with a ladder, and a ranked series of levels is a graded ladder too.

clue.text: Messenger finds boy among crowd

indicators.note: among puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a herd is a crowd, of animals or people
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A courier finds a lad in the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boy' is the stock crossword name Al.
explanation.definitionFit: An official announcer or bearer of news, as in many newspaper titles, is a messenger.

clue.text: Pabus is up about 10 with a quiz

indicators.note: about means around, so the other pieces go inside
in a down answer, being up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so me
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: The setter is awake around ten with a quiz to set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' reverses ME to EM, which goes 'about' X and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination tests knowledge, just as a quiz does.

clue.text: Ric's cocoa, without a question, produces wind

indicators.note: to question something is to call it into doubt, taken here as a signal to shake up these letters
without means removing, so the letter a is taken from the words

explanation.surface: Someone's cocoa, without doubt, gives a man indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the A of 'Ric's cocoa' and 'question' rearranges the rest. This is a less usual spelling of sirocco.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dusty Mediterranean gust blowing from North Africa is a wind.

clue.text: Power and acceleration found in the animal kingdom

parts.note: A is the physics symbol for acceleration

explanation.surface: Physics terms turn up in a study of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-white bear from China is an animal, so it belongs in that kingdom.

clue.text: Confidence in introducing economics lesson after nine

indicators.note: the introductions of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Assurance gained from an economics class after nine o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' takes the first letters of 'economics lesson after nine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash, flair and self-assurance are what this borrowed French term conveys.

clue.text: Peddle backwards to distraction

indicators.note: backwards means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to peddle goods is to flog them, in British slang

explanation.surface: Selling things in reverse would drive you to distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Flog is British slang for sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisure sport played on links is a pastime, something to take the mind off work.
